title: Quarterly Surge Alignment & Autoscale Experiments Roadmap
creator: Marjorie Chen
description: Quarterly planning ticket to align Dedicated pool surge strategies with a focused slate of autoscaling experiments. Goal: reduce excess reserved spend while preserving latency SLAs for tiered customers. This initiative bundles three experiment tracks (prewarm policy adjustments, adaptive warm-pool sizing, and cost-aware routing) and an operational playbook for on-call response during surge events. Outcomes will feed OKR: reduce dedicated unit cost by 8% while keeping P99 inference latency degradation under 10% for production traffic.
acceptance_criteria: Validated experiment harness in staging with synthetic surge scenarios
Canary deploy of adaptive warm-pool sizing in one region with rollback plan
Cost model projection showing >= 6% unit cost improvement at 60% utilization
Runbook updated and oncall rehearsed with incident playbook and SLA thresholds
milestones: 2026-06-02: Cross-region rollout assessment and cost model update
2026-06-20: Final review and OKR signal report
stakeholders: Priya Rao — Eng Manager, Serving Runtime
risks: Latency regression at P99 if batching/kv-cache interactions change under burst
Experiment signal may be noisy — need robust synthetic traffic generators
Capacity fragmentation across tiers could increase ops overhead
Customer objections to automated warm-pool adjustments without explicit guardrails
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Bench & spike (staging) — validate models with synthetic bursts
Phase 1: Canary (single region, non-critical customers) with feature flag
Phase 2: Tiered expansion (enterprise customers on opt-in pilot)
Phase 3: Global rollout with floor/ceiling guardrails and automatic rollback
Fallback: Immediate model routing to baseline pool + incident runbook execution
metrics: Unit cost per 1k tokens (target: -8% vs baseline)
P99 latency delta during surge (target: <10% regression)
Warm-pool utilization (target: increase baseline by 12% during peak)
